messages.content: Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6.

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.content:
The “standard deviation” you’re looking for is the standard error of the sample mean under the null hypothesis.  
It’s calculated as:

\[
SE = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}
\]

where  
\(s = 1.4\) (sample standard deviation) and  
\(n = 40\) (sample size).

\[
SE = \frac{1.4}{\sqrt{40}} \approx \frac{1.4}{6.3249} \approx 0.221
\]

So the standard deviation (standard error) of the null‑hypothesis test statistic is **≈ 0.22**.
message.reasoning:
The user says: "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6."

They want the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test? That might refer to the standard error of the mean under the null hypothesis? Usually, the standard error of the sample mean is sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size). But they mention "null hypothesis test" maybe they want the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the sample mean under the null hypothesis. That would be sigma / sqrt(n). But we don't know population sigma; we have sample standard deviation 1.4. So we can approximate using sample std dev. So standard error = 1.4 / sqrt(40). Let's compute: sqrt(40) ≈ 6.3249. 1.4 / 6.3249 ≈ 0.2213. So standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the mean is about 0.2213.

But the question: "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6." They might want the standard deviation of the test statistic? The test statistic is (sample_mean - population_mean) / (sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size)). The denominator is the standard error. So the standard deviation of the test statistic under null is 1. So maybe they want the standard error. The phrase "standard deviation of the null hypothesis test" is ambiguous. But likely they want the standard error of the mean. So answer: 0.2213.

We can also compute the p-value using the function. But the user didn't ask for p-value. They asked for standard deviation. So we just compute standard error.
